name: Food Manufacturing Pack
description: Food safety and quality audit content: HACCP verification, supplier and co-manufacturer audits, traceability and recall readiness, allergen and labelling controls, prerequisite programmes. Mapped to Codex HACCP, FSMA (21 CFR 117 and Part 1 Subpart S), ISO 22000, BRCGS and FSSAI.
disclaimer: Clause summaries are paraphrased for retrieval and citation only; they are not the authoritative text of the regulations or standards (ISO and BRCGS texts are copyrighted). All entries are draft pending review by a food-safety domain expert.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Conduct a hazard analysis
clauses.summary: Identify potential biological, chemical and physical hazards at each step, assess likelihood and severity, and identify control measures.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Determine critical control points
clauses.summary: Determine the steps at which control is essential to prevent, eliminate or reduce a significant hazard to an acceptable level.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Establish validated critical limits
clauses.summary: Establish critical limits for each CCP and validate that control measures are capable of controlling the hazard.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Monitor control of CCPs
clauses.summary: Establish a system to monitor each CCP against its critical limits, with records signed by the person monitoring.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Corrective actions
clauses.summary: Establish corrective actions to be taken when monitoring indicates a deviation from a critical limit, including disposition of affected product.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Verification
clauses.summary: Establish procedures to verify that the HACCP system is working as intended, including review of monitoring and corrective action records.

clauses.regulation: Codex CXC 1-1969 General Principles of Food Hygiene
clauses.title: Documentation and records
clauses.summary: Establish documentation and record keeping appropriate to the nature and size of the business.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Food safety plan
clauses.summary: The facility must prepare and implement a written food safety plan prepared or overseen by a preventive controls qualified individual.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Hazard analysis
clauses.summary: A written hazard analysis must identify and evaluate known or reasonably foreseeable hazards for each type of food to determine which require a preventive control.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Monitoring
clauses.summary: Preventive controls must be monitored with adequate frequency and monitoring must be documented in records.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Corrective actions and corrections
clauses.summary: Written corrective action procedures must address problems with preventive controls, evaluate affected food and prevent it entering commerce if unsafe, and be documented.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Validation
clauses.summary: Process preventive controls must be validated as adequate to control the hazard, before or shortly after implementation and when changes require it.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Verification of implementation and effectiveness
clauses.summary: Verification includes calibration, product testing and environmental monitoring as appropriate, and review of monitoring and corrective action records within 7 working days.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Sanitary operations
clauses.summary: Plant and equipment must be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition, with effective pest exclusion and safe use of cleaning and sanitising agents.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 117 (FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food)
clauses.title: Supply-chain program: general requirements
clauses.summary: Where a hazard requires a supply-chain-applied control, the program must include supplier approval and appropriate verification activities such as audits, sampling and testing, and record review.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S (FSMA 204 Food Traceability)
clauses.title: Traceability plan
clauses.summary: Persons subject to the rule must maintain a traceability plan describing record procedures, how foods on the Food Traceability List are identified and how traceability lot codes are assigned.

clauses.regulation: 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S (FSMA 204 Food Traceability)
clauses.title: Record maintenance and availability
clauses.summary: Traceability records must be maintained and provided to FDA within 24 hours of request, including as an electronic sortable spreadsheet where required.

clauses.title: Control of externally provided processes, products or services
clauses.summary: The organisation establishes and applies criteria for evaluation, selection, monitoring and re-evaluation of external providers.

clauses.title: Traceability system
clauses.summary: A traceability system identifies incoming material from suppliers and the first stage of distribution of end product; it is verified and tested.

clauses.title: Emergency preparedness and response
clauses.summary: Procedures respond to potential emergencies and incidents that can affect food safety; they are periodically tested where practical.

clauses.title: Hazard analysis
clauses.summary: The food safety team conducts and documents a hazard analysis to determine hazards to be controlled and the control measures required.

clauses.title: Hazard control plan (HACCP/OPRP plan)
clauses.summary: The organisation establishes a hazard control plan with critical limits or action criteria, monitoring, and actions when limits are not met.

clauses.title: Verification related to PRPs and the hazard control plan
clauses.summary: Verification activities confirm PRPs and the hazard control plan are implemented and effective; results are analysed.

clauses.title: Withdrawal / recall
clauses.summary: The organisation can ensure timely withdrawal or recall of potentially unsafe end product, and verifies effectiveness through testing such as mock recalls.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Food safety plan – HACCP
clauses.summary: The company has a fully implemented and effective food safety plan incorporating the Codex HACCP principles.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Supplier and raw material approval and performance monitoring
clauses.summary: Effective supplier approval and monitoring ensures risks from raw materials and outsourced processing are understood and managed.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Traceability
clauses.summary: The site can trace raw material lots through processing to dispatch and back, and tests the system at least annually.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Incident management, product withdrawal and recall
clauses.summary: The site has a plan to manage incidents and enable withdrawal or recall, and tests the procedure at least annually.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Housekeeping and hygiene
clauses.summary: Housekeeping and cleaning systems maintain appropriate standards of hygiene at all times, with verified cleaning procedures.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Pest management
clauses.summary: The site operates a pest management programme to minimise the risk of infestation, with documented inspections and trend analysis.

clauses.regulation: BRCGS Food Safety Issue 9
clauses.title: Management of allergens
clauses.summary: The site has a system to manage allergenic materials that minimises cross-contact and ensures correct allergen labelling.

clauses.regulation: FSS (Licensing & Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations 2011 (India)
clauses.title: General hygienic and sanitary practices
clauses.summary: Food businesses must meet general hygiene and sanitary requirements for premises, equipment, personnel hygiene, cleaning, pest control and records.

clauses.regulation: FSS (Labelling & Display) Regulations 2020 (India)
clauses.title: Declaration of allergens on labels
clauses.summary: Pre-packaged food labels must declare specified allergenic ingredients.

controls.title: HACCP hazard analysis is complete, current and approved
controls.objective: All significant hazards for each product and process step are identified and assessed.
controls.risk: Unidentified hazards leading to unsafe product reaching consumers.
testOfDesign: Inspect the hazard analysis for coverage of all products, process steps, and biological, chemical (incl. allergen) and physical hazards.
Confirm it is approved by the food safety team / PCQI.
testOfEffectiveness: Confirm the hazard analysis was reviewed in the last 12 months and after each process or product change in the period.
checklist: Is the process flow verified on the floor?
Are allergens and foreign-body hazards included?
Was the analysis reviewed after changes?
controls.recommendation: Review the hazard analysis at least annually and on every product or process change, with sign-off by the food safety team / PCQI.

controls.title: CCP critical limits are validated
controls.objective: Each CCP critical limit is supported by validation evidence.
controls.risk: Critical limits that do not control the hazard.
testOfDesign: Inspect validation studies or scientific references for each CCP critical limit (e.g. roasting time/temperature, metal detector sensitivity).
testOfEffectiveness: For each CCP confirm validation is current and covers the equipment and products in use.
checklist: Does every CCP have documented validation?
Is validation repeated after equipment changes?
controls.recommendation: Document validation for every critical limit and revalidate on equipment, recipe or process change.

controls.title: CCP monitoring records are complete and signed
controls.objective: Every CCP is monitored at the defined frequency and records are complete, contemporaneous and signed.
controls.risk: Loss of control at a CCP not detected.
testOfDesign: Inspect monitoring procedures for frequency, method and responsibility for each CCP.
testOfEffectiveness: Select a sample of batch / shift monitoring records and check completeness, readings within limits, and monitor signature.
checklist: Are all readings recorded at the defined frequency?
Is each record signed by the person monitoring?
Are out-of-limit readings linked to a corrective action?
controls.recommendation: Reinforce contemporaneous recording and signature of CCP monitoring and introduce supervisor end-of-shift checks.

controls.title: Corrective action taken for every CCP deviation
controls.objective: Deviations from critical limits trigger documented corrective action and product disposition.
controls.risk: Unsafe product released after a deviation.
testOfDesign: Inspect the corrective action procedure for product hold, evaluation, disposition and root cause.
testOfEffectiveness: For all deviations in the period inspect corrective action records, product hold and disposition decisions.
checklist: Was affected product held and evaluated?
Is disposition approved by QA?
controls.recommendation: Ensure every CCP deviation is logged with product hold, QA-approved disposition and root cause.

controls.title: HACCP verification and record review within 7 working days
controls.objective: Monitoring and corrective action records are reviewed by a qualified person within the required time.
controls.risk: Monitoring failures detected too late to act.
testOfDesign: Inspect the verification schedule and responsibility for record review.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled weeks confirm records were reviewed and signed within 7 working days.
checklist: Is record review within 7 working days?
Are calibrations of CCP instruments current?
controls.recommendation: Track record review timeliness and escalate reviews overdue beyond 7 working days.

controls.title: Suppliers are approved and monitored on risk
controls.objective: Raw materials come only from approved suppliers whose risk is assessed and verified.
controls.risk: Contaminated or adulterated raw materials (e.g. aflatoxin, pesticide residues) entering production.
testOfDesign: Inspect the supplier approval procedure, raw-material risk assessment and approved supplier list.
testOfEffectiveness: Select purchases in the period and confirm the supplier was approved before receipt and verification activities (audit, COA, testing) were current.
checklist: Was each supplier approved before first purchase?
Are high-risk materials tested or audited per plan?
controls.recommendation: Block purchasing from unapproved suppliers in the ERP and schedule verification by raw-material risk.

controls.title: Co-manufacturers are audited on a risk basis
controls.objective: Outsourced processing sites meet the company's food safety requirements.
controls.risk: Unsafe or non-compliant product produced at a third party under the company's brand.
testOfDesign: Inspect the co-manufacturer list, risk rating and audit plan.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled co-manufacturers confirm audits or GFSI certificates are current and findings are closed.
checklist: Is every co-manufacturer audited or certified?
Are audit findings closed?
controls.recommendation: Maintain a risk-based co-manufacturer audit plan and track findings to closure.

controls.title: Traceability records allow one-up/one-down trace within 24 hours
controls.objective: Lot-level records link incoming materials, production and dispatch and can be produced quickly.
controls.risk: Inability to scope a recall, broadening impact and regulatory exposure.
testOfDesign: Inspect the traceability plan, lot code assignment and key data elements captured at receipt, transformation and shipping.
testOfEffectiveness: Perform a trace exercise on sampled finished lots; time it and confirm full mass balance.
checklist: Can the site trace forward and back within 24 hours?
Is mass balance achieved?
controls.recommendation: Capture lot-level key data elements at each step and test traceability against the 24-hour target.

controls.title: Mock recall is tested at least annually
controls.objective: The recall procedure works and the team can execute it in time.
controls.risk: Slow or incomplete recall causing consumer harm and regulatory action.
testOfDesign: Inspect the recall procedure, team, contacts and regulator notification steps.
testOfEffectiveness: Inspect the latest mock recall: scope, time taken, percentage recovered and actions raised.
checklist: Was a mock recall done in the last 12 months?
Were time and recovery targets met?
controls.recommendation: Run mock recalls at least annually with defined time and recovery targets and close resulting actions.

controls.title: Allergen controls prevent cross-contact and mislabelling
controls.objective: Allergens are segregated, cleaned down and correctly declared on labels.
controls.risk: Undeclared allergen causing consumer harm and recall.
testOfDesign: Inspect the allergen matrix, segregation rules, validated changeover cleaning and label approval process.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled allergen changeovers confirm cleaning verification; for sampled products agree label declarations to the recipe and allergen matrix.
checklist: Is cleaning between allergen and non-allergen runs verified?
Do labels declare all allergens in the recipe?
controls.recommendation: Verify allergen changeover cleaning and reconcile labels to recipes before every new label goes live.

controls.title: Cleaning and sanitation programme is followed and verified
controls.objective: Plant and equipment are kept clean and sanitary.
testOfDesign: Inspect the master cleaning schedule and verification methods (visual, ATP, swabs).
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled days confirm cleaning records are complete and verification results within limits.
checklist: Are cleaning records complete?
Are failed swabs re-cleaned and re-tested?
controls.recommendation: Verify cleaning effectiveness routinely and escalate repeat failures.

controls.title: Pest control programme is effective
controls.objective: Pest activity is prevented, detected and acted on.
controls.risk: Infestation and contamination of product or storage.
testOfDesign: Inspect the pest control contract, site map of devices and inspection frequency.
testOfEffectiveness: For sampled months inspect contractor reports, trend analysis and closure of recommendations.
checklist: Are inspections at the contracted frequency?
Are recommendations closed?
controls.recommendation: Trend pest activity monthly and close contractor recommendations within agreed timelines.
